historical_reviews.deepseek: Captures numeric IDs but cannot decide completeness or correct physical devices without an approved inventory and authentic target.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly requires bridges/multifunction/optional-slot policy, full output and no PCIe mutations.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code/source search found no earlier V3.1 record for this identity.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Vendor:device IDs identify functions but not necessarily the intended board or slot; subsystem IDs, class/function count and physical topology are needed where the BOM distinguishes add-in cards sharing a silicon ID.

original_test_intent: Verify that every required PCIe function on the exact SUT enumerates with the expected vendor/device identity and class, with required/optional/absent devices reconciled to the platform BOM and topology.
original_method: Authenticate the SUT and host key, pin the board/BIOS/BOM recipe, collect complete unfiltered numeric PCIe inventory with domain/BDF and full exit status, retain bridges and all multifunction functions, map functions to expected onboard/slot devices using subsystem/topology evidence where necessary, and compare without rescanning or changing PCIe state.
manual_activity: A platform owner approves the expected onboard/slot PCIe BOM and decides optional, hidden or unexpected function discrepancies after automated inventory comparison.
safety_requirements: Do not rescan buses, reset links/devices, bind/unbind drivers or write config space
Do not accept names without numeric IDs
Map shared silicon IDs with subsystem/topology evidence
Stop on wrong host or incomplete access
Preserve raw output and exit status
agent_execution_scope: Parse domain/BDF, class, vendor/device and subsystem when required
engineer_actions: Review missing, duplicate or unexpected functions

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `lspci -nn` is the correct basic observation, but insecure transport and the absence of a machine-readable expected inventory make `user verifies` unauditable.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Through verified-host SSH, capture complete numeric PCIe inventory (including domain and sufficient verbose/subsystem context when the BOM needs it) with exit status, without filters or mutations.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The `lspci -nn` device/vendor objective and 40-minute activity remain; authentication, topology mapping and comparison evidence are added.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create an expected-versus-observed table keyed by physical role and domain:BDF, with class, vendor:device, subsystem IDs, function count and required/optional disposition.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds physical/BOM semantics and complete function accounting beyond a raw name list.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A correct vendor/device ID can belong to the wrong slot/card revision, while a missing secondary function or unexpected bridge can be hidden in an unstructured list.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: BDFs may change across firmware or topology changes; physical role should not be inferred from BDF unless the recipe explicitly fixes it.

project_override_considerations: Define required, optional and forbidden functions, subsystem-ID and physical-slot mapping, bridge inclusion, SR-IOV/virtual-function state and whether domain-qualified BDFs are part of acceptance.
expected_evidence: Complete numeric inventory with domain:BDF and exit status
Parsed function table including class/vendor/device and required subsystem data

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, procedure and criteria consistently request PCIe device/vendor inventory. DeepSeek's transport and comparison omissions are execution defects.

blocked_analysis.analysis: BOM, topology, access and optional-device policy are identifiable inputs. Execution becomes BLOCKED only if complete enumeration or mapping to required physical roles cannot be established.

review_improvement: Turns a raw numeric list into a complete, physical-role-aware PCIe function inventory while explicitly avoiding unstable BDF assumptions.
independent_technical_reasoning: PCIe enumeration is function-level: one card can expose several functions, and different cards can reuse the same silicon vendor/device IDs. Therefore device/vendor matching alone cannot prove the installed BOM; function count, subsystem identity and topology/slot role must close the identity chain.
